relevance_note: Single case report of a GAMT-deficient patient with a printed GAMT variant: "a homozygous pathogenic variant of c.327G>A silent mutation was found in the GAMT gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans; values were written by me. Two in-scope people: the case-report patient (label 'patient', rule 5) and one previously published patient from the Discussion with an individual-level feature ('1 study reported a patient with recurrent bone fractures ... [17]', label 'ref [17] patient', rule 4); that person has no variant, sex or age in this paper. The '3 patients with a family history of GAMT deficiency ... [19,29,31]' are a group statement citing several papers with no individual-level detail, so they get no rows. Table 1 has empty first-column cells for rows that continue the previous age; onset was taken only from rows with their own age cell (e.g. 'Developmental delay', 'ADHD' have empty age cells and get no onset). Seizure onset '5-12 y' is a range, so no ISO duration. Age at last evaluation taken from the age-17 MRI ('At age 17'). Age at onset taken as the first Table 1 symptom (6 mo failure to thrive); the paper does not label an overall onset age. Normal findings recorded under D-27: CPK normal -> elevated CPK excluded; TSH normal -> abnormal TSH excluded; comprehensive metabolic panel normal written as a whole panel ('abnormal comprehensive metabolic panel' excluded), excluding nothing more specific; head circumference 50th percentile -> microcephaly and macrocephaly excluded; 'good eye contact' -> poor eye contact excluded (does not exclude the broader autistic-features checklist item, which is observed from 'Autism' at 5 y); fetal movement normal -> abnormal fetal movement excluded. The early brain MRI (around 19 months) 'was normal' is recorded as 'abnormal brain MRI' excluded for that time only; it is a whole-investigation statement and excludes no specific MRI checklist item; the age-17 MRI showed volume loss and ventricular/sulcal prominence. MR spectroscopy voxel over 'normal-appearing white matter of right centrum semiovale' was not used to exclude white matter abnormalities (regional, narrower than the checklist item). EEG 'was unable to be obtained', so abnormal EEG is not reported. Hair pulling and biting are recorded as stated; the paper does not say whether they were self-directed or aimed at others, so self-injurious and aggressive behaviour are not reported. Hyperactivity checklist item marked observed from the table entry 'ADHD'. Absent or limited speech left not reported: the paper gives minimal babbling at 10 months and a language age of 13 mo at 3 y, but no statement of absent or limited speech. Variant type: the patient's sentence calls c.327G>A a 'silent mutation', recorded as 'other'; the Introduction's remark that the variant 'occurs at the second exon splice site' is about 'Many patients' in general, not this person, so 'splice' was not used. Genetic testing at 3 years 'showed no abnormalities'; repeat testing at 12 found the variant. Vital status not stated explicitly (left not reported). Maternal pregnancy factors (anemia, alcohol, tobacco) are not the patient's features and were not recorded. Non-breaking spaces in Table 1 cells ('Gross motor = 18 mo' etc.) are kept in the spans. No contradictions found in the paper.

treatment_summary.value: multiple seizure medications trialed, none effective; from age 14 creatine monohydrate 800 mg/kg/day and ornithine 800 mg/kg/day, continued; arginine not restricted
span: Multiple seizure medications were trialed, however none proved effective.
at the age of 14 the patient was started on creatine monohydrate at 800 mg/kg of body weight per day, and ornithine supplementation at 800 mg/kg of body weight per day
The patient has since continued to supplement creatine and ornithine at the same rate as it previously showed clinical improvement.
The patient opted not to restrict arginine from the diet.

disease_label_as_stated.span: diagnosing the patient with pathogenic GAMT deficiency, a cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing at age 12 (homozygous pathogenic c.327G>A in GAMT; earlier genetic testing at age 3 showed no abnormalities); MR spectroscopy reduced creatine peak further confirmed the diagnosis
span: repeat genetic testing at age 12 was obtained. Results showed a homozygous pathogenic variant of c.327G>A silent mutation was found in the GAMT gene, diagnosing the patient with pathogenic GAMT deficiency
Genetic testing performed at 3 years of age showed no abnormalities.
MR Spectroscopy further confirmed the diagnosis in our case by showing a reduced creatine peak within the brain parenchyma.
